top_categories.workout_context: 1553 miles. Your legs will beg to quit after 120. This trains the power output you need from mile 130 onward.

Race Across France's mixed terrain rewards road-specific control. Practice smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 1553 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Race Across France's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before June.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 1553 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
At Race Across France, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
1553 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.
93,832ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
60ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
93,832ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 93,832ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Race Across France. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Race Across France. Train it until it feels boring.

race_overlay.heat: June in Hendaye to Mandelieu-la-Napoule, France can bring heat. Complete 3–4 heat exposure sessions in the final 2 weeks before Race Across France. Increase sodium intake 48 hours before race day.
race_overlay.nutrition: Ultra-distance fueling for 1553 miles requires a practiced resupply plan built around confirmed course services and available commercial stops. Rehearse frequent carbohydrate intake on long rides, then scale the plan to intensity, sleep strategy, tolerance, and real food across the full event. Carry redundant fuel and avoid applying a short-event hourly target or fixed total-calorie estimate to a multi-day race.
race_overlay.altitude: Altitude may change sustainable power and recovery at Race Across France. Use conservative pacing and test any travel strategy before the event.
race_overlay.terrain: Highly technical terrain at Race Across France demands practice on similar surfaces. Ride mixed terrain at race-day cadence weekly. Practice cornering, descending, and power delivery on unstable surfaces. Dial in tire pressure before race week — 5 PSI wrong costs you 15+ minutes over 1553 miles.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, Road Specific, and Race Simulation to prepare you for 1553 miles of mixed terrain in Hendaye to Mandelieu-la-Napoule, France.
